Key Research Thinking Patterns: Cost-Driven Materials Engineering: Selecting and designing materials primarily to overcome a critical cost barrier in an existing technology. (e.g., The researchers chose IV-VI semiconductor alloys (PbSnSe/PbSrSe) because they can be grown on "low cost silicon substrates", aiming to solve the high-cost problem of traditional III-V TPV devices that require expensive substrates).

Band Structure Engineering: Using quantum confinement principles to intentionally modify a material's electronic properties to achieve a specific performance goal. (e.g., The researchers used multiple quantum wells (MQWs) to "remove L-valley degeneracy". This quantum effect reduces the material's density of states, which in turn decreases reverse saturation currents and "increases open circuit voltage", solving a known flaw in bulk IV-VI semiconductors).

System-Level Optimization and Economic Modeling: Designing a multi-component device by optimizing its parameters for a specific operational system and evaluating its viability with a real-world economic framework. (e.g., The researchers designed triple-junction TPV devices with specific bandgaps (707, 559, and 443 meV) to match the emission spectrum of a 1400°C radiator. They then optimized layer thicknesses for "current-matching" and used the resulting performance (power generation and efficiency) in a "levelized cost of energy (LCOE) calculation" to prove the economic competitiveness of the entire thermal storage system).

Proxy-Based Biomarker Sensing: Identifying a measurable, downstream chemical (a proxy) to non-invasively monitor a complex, difficult-to-measure biological process. (e.g., The researchers identified volatile acetaldehyde as a measurable proxy for elevated pyruvate concentrations in cancer cells. They then used a mid-IR laser to measure this gas-phase acetaldehyde to observe "HIF-1α driven shifts in cancer cell metabolism", which is the complex biological process of interest).
Summary Description: Dr. Patrick McCann specializes in IV-VI semiconductor physics, exploring the interplay between materials science and energy conversion, particularly in thermophotovoltaics (TPV). His research focuses on designing and modeling PbSnSe/PbSrSe multiple quantum well (MQW) structures grown on low-cost silicon substrates. He applies techniques like band structure engineering, leveraging quantum confinement to remove L-valley degeneracy and enhance TPV device performance. This work is often contextualized with system-level economic modeling, like Levelized Cost of Energy (LCOE) analysis, for molten silicon thermal energy storage. His expertise also extends to mid-IR optoelectronics, utilizing Interband Cascade Lasers (ICLs) for high-sensitivity trace gas sensing in bioanalytical applications, such as monitoring acetaldehyde from breast cancer cell metabolism.
